run.rulesInOwnWords: 1) Charge: add the cycle's charge-table row to each form; capacity is ignored here. 2) Overtop: go through forms 1 to 6 in order. If a form holds more than its volume, move the excess to the next form, so it can cascade within the same pass. Excess from form 6 goes to waste. 3) Status, using contents after overtop: GREEN with at least the upper mark (>= upper) becomes HOT. HOT with at most the lower mark (<= lower) becomes GREEN. Anything else keeps its status, which gives hysteresis. Each form changes at most once per cycle. 4) Settle: first compute all six amounts from the current contents. GREEN gives floor(x/4) and HOT gives floor(x/2). Then apply them at the same time. Every form loses its amount. A GREEN form's amount goes to waste. A HOT form's amount goes to form n-1, except form 1, whose amount goes to waste. A form can end above its volume, and that excess is only handled at the next cycle's overtop (in cycle 5 it stays). 5) Washout: if the total of the six forms is greater than 38, every form becomes floor(x/2) and the removed units go to waste. A total of exactly 38 does not fire. Waste tally starts at 0. Balance check: start total plus all charges = end total plus waste.
